title: Dural Cell Isolation
author: Andrea Argouarch
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8ghhtt6
materials: Aspirate biohazard media and throw away biohazard materials properly

steps.title: Autoclave coverslips and tools
steps.instruction: Place 25 mm round coverslips (7 per 13 cm autoclave pouch, catalog #GG-25) and one each of surgical tools (Dumont #5 forceps, Fine Science Tools catalog #11251‑30; tungsten carbide scissors, Fine Science Tools catalog #14568‑12) into separate 23 cm autoclave pouches, seal each pouch with an Instant Sealing Sterilization Pouch (3.5 × 9 in., catalog #0181251 or 3.5 × 5 in., catalog #0181250), autoclave, and verify that the autoclave tape has turned black.

steps.title: Turn off UV and clean hood
steps.instruction: Turn off the UV lights in the biosafety hood and wipe the interior surfaces with 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Prepare reagents and consumables
steps.instruction: Gather and label all consumables: DPBS -/- (no Ca²⁺, no Mg²⁺, Thermo Fisher catalog #14190250); sterile filtered fibroblast media consisting of high‑glucose DMEM with sodium pyruvate (1×, Thermo Fisher catalog #11995073), 10 % heat‑inactivated FBS (VWR catalog #97068‑091), and 1 % PenStrep (Thermo Fisher catalog #15140122). Set up a 10 cm dish labeled “dirty” for the biopsy, a 6‑well plate for washes (wells 1‑4, each filled with 3 mL DPBS -/-), a 10 cm dish labeled “clean” with ~15 mL fresh fibroblast media, a 10 cm plate labeled “tools”, a 6‑well plate labeled with ID, date, and passage (p0), autoclaved 25 mm coverslips, autoclaved surgical tools, and 3‑4 Nalgene cryogenic vials (catalog #66008‑706) pre‑labeled (date, ID, Dura Tissue). Prepare 1 mL of freezing media per vial (10 % DMSO final concentration using Bio‑Max Cell Culture Grade DMSO, catalog #40470005‑2, mixed with 90 % of the fibroblast media).

steps.title: Transfer biopsy to dirty dish
steps.instruction: In the hood, spray the dural biopsy into the biosafety cabinet and pour the media containing the biopsy into the “dirty” 10 cm dish.

steps.title: Rinse biopsy through DPBS wells
steps.instruction: Using sterile forceps, submerge the biopsy in DPBS well 1, tilt, rinse, and swirl for 1 minute; repeat sequentially in wells 2, 3, and 4, each for 1 minute.

steps.title: Move biopsy to clean dish
steps.instruction: With forceps, transfer the rinsed biopsy into the “clean” 10 cm dish containing ~15 mL fresh fibroblast media, keeping the tissue fully submerged.

steps.title: Section biopsy for freezing and culture
steps.instruction: Cut the biopsy into 3‑5 regions. Place 2‑4 sections into the pre‑labeled LN₂ vials (avoid touching the outside of the vials), add 1 mL freezing media to each, and store the vials in a Mr. Frosty at –80 °C for 25‑48 hours. After this period, transfer the vials to liquid nitrogen (≈ –190 °C) for long‑term storage. Reserve the remaining section for immediate culture.

steps.title: Mince culture section into pin‑head pieces
steps.instruction: Using tweezers, forceps, and tungsten scissors, cut the reserved biopsy section into ~18‑20 pin‑head‑sized pieces, keeping the tissue moist and preventing drying.

steps.title: Seed tissue pieces onto coverslips
steps.instruction: In each well of a 6‑well plate, place a 200 µL droplet of fibroblast media in the center, add several similarly sized tissue pieces into the droplet, then gently lay an autoclaved 25 mm coverslip over the droplet, starting from one side, centering it, and avoiding air bubbles.

steps.title: Press coverslip and add media
steps.instruction: Gently press the coverslip so the tissue adheres evenly and firmly (flat, no wobble, tissue slightly flattened but dense). Then add 3 mL of fibroblast media to each well, placing forceps on top of the coverslip to keep it down and adding the media quickly to break surface tension.

steps.title: Inspect and incubate
steps.instruction: Observe tissue integrity under a microscope, then place the 6‑well plate in a 37 °C incubator with 5 % CO₂. Do not move the plate for the first week; allow the tissue to settle for one week before the first media change, monitoring cell growth.

steps.title: Clean surgical tools for reuse
steps.instruction: Brush the surgical tools with 409 soap water, rinse with water, dry on kimwipes, rinse with 100 % ethanol, and dry completely with kimwipes to prevent rust or water marks. Wear a waterproof lab coat and eye protection/PPE, and set the cleaned tools aside for the next autoclave cycle.

steps.title: Decontaminate hood and record
steps.instruction: Clean and sterilize the biosafety hood with 70 % ethanol, turn the UV lights back on, and update the cell‑culture notes in the lab notebook.
